coaching.headline: A 1-8 tower loss: two fights won and cashed none, four fights lost and every one converted against us.
coaching.team: Lanes split down the middle: mid controlled Wraith the entire game, the carry and offlane matchups were roughly even, and the jungle lane was lost to Serath the entire game while the support lane was lost early to Riktor before evening out later. The 12-minute and 16.9-minute fights were both lost outright and fed an enemy Fangtooth, an outer tower, and a second Fangtooth. The two fights we did win, at 7.7 and 22.2 minutes, never turned into one of our own objectives — the 22.2 win even traded three kills for the enemy's Fangtooth anyway. By 26 minutes, the enemy took Orb Prime with nobody on our team dead to explain it — we simply weren't there to contest it. The fight taken right after, at 26.3 minutes and at full strength, was lost 1-5, opening the inner tower, both inhibitors, and the core. Vision told the same story: 26 wards placed to the other side's 39. That's part of a pattern worth fixing next game — three separate fights this game had a teammate alive and ahead in their own lane who never rotated in; making that rotation happen before the fight starts, not after, is the one change worth carrying forward.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The clearest split in the box score is conversion: we won two fights and turned zero of them into one of our own objectives, while the four fights the enemy won became two Fangtooths and multiple towers. The Orb Prime at 26 minutes was the sharpest example — nobody on our team was even dead when it was taken, meaning it wasn't lost in a fight, it was left uncontested. Engaging at full strength right after that, at 26.3 minutes, turned into a 1-5 loss that opened the inner tower, both inhibitors, and the core.
coaching.whatWorked: Greystone's offlane matchup against Aurora produced three kills, at 5.5, 7.8, and 12.7 minutes, and Greystone was the only one of the five who carried a magic-resist item into a comp built around Aurora's 36,529 magic damage — the one piece of the counter-build plan that actually got executed.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31's Maco lost the early support lane to Riktor and got caught alone at the 10-minute mark, with nobody around to punish the pick before it happened. He found the game's one clean trade later, taking down Dekker in the fight at 18.5 minutes, but his other three deaths — at 16.9, 24.8, and the final one at 27 — all landed inside fights the team lost outright, each feeding straight into a tower or Fangtooth for the other side.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324's Kira closed the Dekker matchup from behind, going down to Dekker at 14.3 minutes before finishing the trade at 21.7. The fight at 18.5 minutes was fought a body down while her own lane sat ahead — the rotation that would have evened the numbers never came — and three of her four deaths landed inside fights the team was already losing.
perPlayer.6317c922-6a5c-4287-a2a3-24a24aa25bfa: The offlane Greystone conceded first blood alone to Serath at 2.2 minutes, then got caught alone twice more before 20 minutes — three solo deaths is the offlane story here more than any farm number. The matchup itself swung the other way over time: Greystone took down Aurora three times across the game and was the only one of the five who itemized magic resist against a comp built around her damage.
perPlayer.dd5a8477-4c5d-4f67-a8af-66eea1569e4f: Boris lost the jungle matchup to Serath for the entire game, and it shows in the death count — nine deaths, the most on the roster, including getting caught alone by Serath at 20.3 minutes. His deaths at 12 and 17.2 minutes each preceded an enemy Fangtooth or tower within the next couple of minutes, so the lost jungle matchup wasn't just a lane problem, it kept costing map objectives too.
perPlayer.495fb001-0cda-4f3b-b23a-24a4859af934: Iggy & Scorch won the mid lane against Wraith for the entire game and still finished with zero kills across seven deaths, with only two items completed by the time the game ended at 27 minutes. Three of those deaths each preceded a Fangtooth or Orb Prime taken by the other side soon after — a favored lane that never turned into pressure on the map.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.text: One kill, one cheap solo death to Riktor at 10 minutes, and three more deaths inside fights the team was already losing. Support is not graded on the kill line: the healing and assists were real, and the vision fight still went to the other side, 26 wards placed to their 39.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.text: Closed the Dekker matchup from behind, exactly as the lane read (theirs early, ours late) predicted. The 18.5-minute fight going a body down while her lane sat ahead is the one clean what-if of the game.

6317c922-6a5c-4287-a2a3-24a24aa25bfa.text: Three kills on Aurora and the only magic-resist item on the roster against a magic-heavy enemy comp are real strengths. Getting caught alone three separate times, including first blood at 2.2 minutes, is the other half — for an offlane, three solo deaths is the headline stat here, ahead of any farm number.

dd5a8477-4c5d-4f67-a8af-66eea1569e4f.text: Nine deaths is the most on the roster, in a jungle matchup that was unfavored the entire game against Serath. Two of those deaths, at 12 and 17.2 minutes, each preceded an enemy Fangtooth or tower within two minutes — the lane loss kept costing map objectives, not just kills.

495fb001-0cda-4f3b-b23a-24a4859af934.text: Won the mid lane against Wraith the whole game and still finished zero kills across seven deaths, with only two items done by the 27-minute mark. Several of those deaths fed a Fangtooth or Orb Prime soon after — a favored lane that never turned into pressure.

16.9.call: The 16.9-minute fight went 0-3 with two teammates not there: the offlane was alive but never made it, and the midlane was alive and ahead in its own lane but never rotated in either. Either one showing up flips the numbers; instead, the loss fed both the outer tower and the Fangtooth that followed at 18.1 minutes.

24.4.call: At 24.4 minutes the team fought 1-4 while the offlane, ahead in its own lane, never rotated in. The loss gave up an outer tower, and the Orb Prime fell soon after, at 25.6 minutes, uncontested — nobody on our side was dead when it was taken.

26.3.call: The Orb Prime at 26 minutes was conceded with nobody on the team dead to explain it — it simply wasn't contested. The full squad engaged anyway at 26.3 minutes, lost 1-5, and that fight opened the inner tower, both inhibitors, and the core that ended the game.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Maco built for mana and self-sustain — Hexbound Bracers, Everbloom, and Timewarp all lean into health, mana, and cooldown stats — instead of the trio the winning games ran: Crescelia, Enra's Blessing, and Windcaller. The gap that mattered most is Enra's Blessing, which shields an ally the instant they get locked down; Everbloom's own defensive proc triggers off a heal, not off crowd control, so it doesn't answer Riktor's pull-into-silence the same way. Maco also carried no magic resist into a comp that ran three magical damage-dealers.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: The engine's top pick for Maco is Vesh, whose major layers a burn onto every ability hit that lands — a fit for a kit that's constantly poking with Gift! and Fly!, and the minor pairing turns that burn into more damage against tankier targets while speeding up cooldowns off every takedown. It doesn't add any durability, though, and that's the gap that mattered: Maco's own low survivability is a known weakness of the kit, and it's exactly what let Riktor catch him alone at 10 minutes and again inside three of the fights the team lost.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Kira built a crit-and-attack-speed kit — Vanquisher, Onixian Quiver, Scattershot — instead of the winning trio of Solaris, Ashbringer, and Imperator. That trio's difference is a sustain-and-tempo loop: an empowered hit that heals back a share of what Kira deals, plus cooldown refunds on every hit that speed up her stack-and-channel routine. Against a comp with a pull-and-suppress support and a diving jungler, that self-healing and faster ability loop is exactly what keeps a channeling marksman alive through the window her ultimate needs; the built path traded that for pure damage output instead.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Kira's top pick, Demiurge, inflates whatever her completed items already give her — stats and item-effect damage both — which rewards exactly the crit/attack-speed build she ran. Its minors lean into surviving long enough to cash that in: bonus health and haste as she levels, plus more damage and defense the more items she finishes. The trade is that it's weak before the build is online, which lines up with the lane read of theirs early, ours late against Dekker — the eternal's value, like the item build, only shows up once a few completed items are in.

6317c922-6a5c-4287-a2a3-24a24aa25bfa.build: Greystone landed on the actual winning core — Overlord, Rapture, and Aegis Of Agawar — then added Catalytic Drive as a fourth item rather than more offense. That pickup is the one build decision worth crediting: Catalytic Drive is a magic-resist item with an execute-and-heal proc, exactly what a frontline needed against a comp anchored by Aurora's magic damage, and Greystone was the only one of the five to carry any magic resist at all.
6317c922-6a5c-4287-a2a3-24a24aa25bfa.eternal: Greystone's top pick, Krix, grows his max health every level and adds size to match — a direct fit for a frontline whose plan is to soak damage and reset fights with a stasis ultimate. The minor pairing cuts healing on whatever his damage-over-time touches and permanently adds health for every takedown, which lines up with taking down Aurora three times over the game. It's a durability and attrition pick rather than a damage one, which fits an offlane matchup that started in Aurora's favor early and only turned to Greystone's favor as the game went on.

dd5a8477-4c5d-4f67-a8af-66eea1569e4f.build: Boris ran Sky Splitter, Tainted Blade, and Rapture — one slot short of the winning core's Basilisk, an armor-shred item that stacks up over a fight and snowballs a jungler's picks. Tainted Blade's healing-cut was arguably the more urgent need — the team carried only one source of it all game against a comp with a healer — so that slot wasn't wasted, but neither option adds magic resist, and Boris, like Maco, went the whole game without any against a comp that ran three magical damage-dealers.
dd5a8477-4c5d-4f67-a8af-66eea1569e4f.eternal: Boris's top pick is also Demiurge, which inflates whatever his finished items already grant — relevant for a jungle tank that leans on a handful of completed items to be a real threat. Its minors add health and haste as he levels plus more damage and defense the more of the build is done, rewarding a jungler who's fully built and still online late. The catch is the same scaling trade as Kira's: it's weak before the build finishes, and Boris only had three items done — Basilisk, the missing piece of the winning core, was never bought — by the time the game ended.

495fb001-0cda-4f3b-b23a-24a4859af934.build: Only two items were finished by the loss — Orb Of Enlightenment and Megacosm — with Entropy, the third piece of the winning core, never completed. Entropy's role is more magic power and mana plus a touch of extra damage on every spell hit, which stacks well with a kit that's already applying a damage-over-time effect with every basic attack. The bigger issue is simply that a 27-minute game only produced two completed items in a lane that was won the entire game, so the lane advantage never turned into itemized power.
495fb001-0cda-4f3b-b23a-24a4859af934.eternal: Iggy & Scorch's top pick is also Demiurge, boosting whatever his finished items grant plus the damage those item effects deal — which stacks with a kit built around layering damage-over-time zones. The minors add health and cooldown speed as he levels and more damage and defense per item owned, again rewarding a finished build. That's the exact problem here: only two items were finished by the loss, so most of what Demiurge offers — and most of the mid lane advantage he held all game — never had anything to scale off.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~2.5s of lockdown): Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Riktor. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Maco) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
